requirement: Two normally closed master valves in series: valve A powered only by the safety monitor, valve B only by the thrust control unit
Arming requires Track mode, a physical arm switch, zone authorisation from two independent sources, speed and wind within limits, belts fastened and a clear zone
A leak-down test of the master valves runs at every power-on; a failure locks out thrust
Thrust messages are authenticated; production cars have no remote thrust path
Pressure is measured by two dissimilar sensors per gas group, with temperature compensation
COPVs meet a burst ratio of 2.25 or more and pass pressure-cycling, fire, drop and impact tests equivalent to UN GTR 13
On crash detection all vessel valves close within 50 ms; venting only through thrust-neutral diffusers away from the cabin
Loss of suction is detected from plenum pressure and speed and cornering limits apply within 100 ms, with a warning
A stuck-open thruster valve is detected and its line isolated within 20 ms (hard ceiling 50 ms)
A hop starts only if usable gas is at least 1.2 times the predicted need, corrected for mass and gas temperature; otherwise a lower manoeuvre is offered
If predicted gas at landing falls below the reserve mid-manoeuvre, recovery starts at once: level attitude first, then land
While airborne the safety monitor commands recovery instead of closing the master valves, unless thrust itself is the uncontainable fault
Attitude comes from three IMUs with voting; the monitor checks it with a dissimilar sensor
External airbags arm only in Hop mode above 1.5 m and are disarmed by two independent signals on landing
After isolating any one lift group, the remaining torque-balanced groups lift at least 1.1 times maximum vehicle weight (about 10 kN per group)
Before every arming each thruster, line and master valve is cycled against a pressurised test volume; coverage of stuck-open and stuck-closed faults at least 99.9%
Any single stuck-closed nozzle leaves at least 50% of nominal roll-braking authority (individually controlled nozzles)
COPVs, valves and seals are qualified to the lowest gas temperature of a full discharge, or discharge is limited to their qualified temperature
Refill air is dried to a dew point below -40 C, checked at the coupling; otherwise the fill is refused
The recovery planner chooses the upright attitude reachable with the least altitude loss, using the predicted stopping angle
In Hop mode no single loss of power, coil, switch or computer closes a master valve for at least 5 s (dual-wound coils, second driver, hold-up energy); closing in flight needs an explicit command
Hop-mode control is fail-operational for at least 5 s: a backup attitude-hold and descent law on independent hardware takes over within 50 ms
Thruster and line valve commands are direct-wired or carried on two independent buses; a lost command opens nothing new
